summary: Tista Biswas is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami. As attested in 2026, she served at The Asiatic Society as Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies.
Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd A. Gibson works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, attested in 1991, and studied under György Kara.

Todd Thornton Lewis works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under mentors and teachers including Margaret Mead and Alex Wayman, later serving as Murray Distinguished Professor at the College of the Holy Cross.

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor David Pingree in 2008 as well as Kim Plofker.

Tokio Takata is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1997–2014) and special appointed professor at Fudan University (2016–2022).

Tokiyoshi Hōjō (1858–1929) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1880–1885). He taught Kitaro Nishida and held positions at Yamaguchi University (~1894–1896), Kanazawa University (~1898–1908), and Tohoku University (~1913–1917).

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa and Kyoto universities and under Kodo Sawaki (1941). He served at Komazawa University (1949–1987) as professor emeritus and as lecturer at Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Junjirō Takakusu and Gaju Ikehara. He held teaching posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University, University of Freiburg, and under Kitaro Nishida and Martin Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University (1925–1943), Kyoto University (1931–1953), and Ryukoku University (1961).
Tom De Rauw is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Ann Heirman. As of 2026, he held an AAP post at Ghent University.

Tom Ginsburg is a scholar of law, political science, and Buddhist studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1985–1999). He taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before becoming Leo Spitz Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago.

Tom Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Lausanne and as Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.
Tomohiro Manabe is an Indologist and philosopher. He held a lecturer post at Waseda University (attested 2020) and serves as an associate professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Tomoko Makidono works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She was a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale (~1977–1979), and UC Santa Barbara (~1979–1985), later holding faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–1999) and the University of Michigan (1999).
Tomomichi Nitta works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a full-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012) and as a professor at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima is an Indologist who studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012). He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He also served at Taisho University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
